deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no mathematics by Ramanujan. It is a later archival or editorial cover slip, in a non-Ramanujan hand, attached to the manuscript. It reads:
(i) 'with Add. Ms. a.94 18(20)', a shelf-mark cross-reference.
(ii) 'Incomplete?'
(iii) 'Intended as conclusion to "Certain Trigonometrical Sums" 21. p.129.' This refers to Ramanujan's paper 'On certain trigonometrical sums and their applications in the theory of numbers', Trans. Camb. Phil. Soc. 22 (1918). It is no. 21 in the Collected Papers. The page reference as written looks like '129'; since that paper begins on p.179 of the Collected Papers, '179' may be meant, but this is uncertain.
(iv) A struck-through sentence: 'Does not seem to do find Σ_1^∞ r_s(n)x^n or Σ_1^∞ σ_s(n)x^n as it sets out to do.'
(v) 'Last 2 pages scraps on the same subject.'

Context from the neighbouring pages: the manuscript is a §18 meant to close the trigonometrical-sums paper. It sets out to find expressions for Σσ_s(n)x^n and Σr_s(n)x^n that show their asymptotic behaviour for large s. The steps are:
1. Start from the partial-fraction expansion of π coth(πx) (18.1).
2. Differentiate s−1 times to get the Lipschitz-type formula (18.11): Σ n^{s-1} e^{-2πnx} = Γ(s)/(2π)^s Σ_{k∈Z} (x+ik)^{-s}.
3. Replace x by nx and sum over n. This gives the Eisenstein-series expression (18.2) for Σσ_{s-1}(n)e^{-2πnx}, with a sum over coprime pairs (μ,ν) multiplied by ζ(s).
4. Specialise to x=1 (18.3) and x=(√3+i)/2 (18.4).

The slip's (struck-out) remark is the cataloguer's judgment that the manuscript breaks off before reaching the generating functions promised in its opening sentence.
errors: No mathematical content on this page, so nothing to check.

The cataloguer's remark that the manuscript does not find Σσ_s(n)x^n is arguably too strong. Formula (18.2) on the neighbouring pages does give Σσ_{s-1}(n)e^{-2πnx} as an Eisenstein-type lattice sum. It is the r_s(n) part that is not reached in the extant pages.
The page reference '21. p.129' may be a slip or misreading for p.179, the opening page of paper 21 in the Collected Papers; this is uncertain.

The underlying mathematics on adjacent pages is the Lipschitz summation formula and the expression of Σσ_{s-1}(n)q^n via Eisenstein series over coprime lattice points.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a librarian's or editor's cover slip with no mathematics. The manuscript it describes has been discussed in the literature, e.g. in Andrews–Berndt's editions of Ramanujan's unpublished manuscripts and lost notebook, and its content is classical.

checkable.asserts: Lipschitz formula (18.11) from the adjacent page, at s=4, x=1. The truncated lattice sum makes this approximate.
